verses.text: Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets, and said to him, “Put your belt on your waist, take this vial of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth Gilead.
When you come there, find Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi, and go in, and make him rise up from among his brothers, and take him to an inner room.
Then take the vial of oil, and pour it on his head, and say, ‘Yahweh says, “I have anointed you king over Israel.”’ Then open the door, flee, and don’t wait.”
So the young man, even the young man, the prophet, went to Ramoth Gilead.
When he came, behold, the captains of the army were sitting. Then he said, “I have a message for you, captain.” Jehu said, “To which of us all?” He said, “To you, O captain.”
He arose, and went into the house. Then he poured the oil on his head, and said to him, “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, ‘I have anointed you king over the people of Yahweh, even over Israel.
You must strike your master Ahab’s house, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of Yahweh, at the hand of Jezebel.
For the whole house of Ahab will perish. I will cut off from Ahab everyone who urinates against a wall,  both him who is shut up and him who is left at large in Israel.
I will make Ahab’s house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah.
The dogs will eat Jezebel on the plot of ground of Jezreel, and there shall be no one to bury her.’” Then he opened the door and fled.
When Jehu came out to the servants of his lord, and one said to him, “Is all well? Why did this mad fellow come to you?” He said to them, “You know the man and how he talks.”
They said, “That is a lie. Tell us now.” He said, “He said to me, ‘Yahweh says, I have anointed you king over Israel.’”
Then they hurried, and each man took his cloak, and put it under him on the top of the stairs, and blew the trumpet, saying, “Jehu is king.”
So Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. (Now Joram was keeping Ramoth Gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael king of Syria;

but king Joram had returned to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which the Syrians had given him, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria.) Jehu said, “If this is your thinking, then let no one escape and go out of the city, to go to tell it in Jezreel.”
So Jehu rode in a chariot and went to Jezreel, for Joram lay there. Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see Joram.

Now the watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he spied the company of Jehu as he came, and said, “I see a company.” Joram said, “Take a horseman, and send to meet them, and let him say, ‘Is it peace?’”

So one went on horseback to meet him, and said, “Thus says the king, ‘Is it peace?’” Jehu said, “What do you have to do with peace? Fall in behind me!” The watchman said, “The messenger came to them, but he isn’t coming back.”
Then he sent out a second on horseback, who came to them, and said, “Thus says the king, ‘Is it peace?’” Jehu answered, “What do you have to do with peace? Fall in behind me!”
The watchman said, “He came to them, and isn’t coming back. The driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi, for he drives furiously.”

Joram said, “Get ready!” They got his chariot ready. Then Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot, and they went out to meet Jehu, and found him on Naboth the Jezreelite’s land.
When Joram saw Jehu, he said, “Is it peace, Jehu?” He answered, “What peace, so long as the prostitution of your mother Jezebel and her witchcraft abound?”
Joram turned his hands, and fled, and said to Ahaziah, “This is treason, Ahaziah!”
Jehu drew his bow with his full strength, and struck Joram between his arms; and the arrow went out at his heart, and he sunk down in his chariot.

Then Jehu said to Bidkar his captain, “Pick him up, and throw him in the plot of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite; for remember how, when you and I rode together after Ahab his father, Yahweh laid this burden on him:

‘Surely I have seen yesterday the blood of Naboth, and the blood of his sons,’ says Yahweh; ‘and I will repay you in this plot of ground,’ says Yahweh. Now therefore take and cast him onto the plot of ground, according to Yahweh’s word.”

But when Ahaziah the king of Judah saw this, he fled by the way of the garden house. Jehu followed after him, and said, “Strike him also in the chariot!” They struck him at the ascent of Gur, which is by Ibleam. He fled to Megiddo, and died there.
His servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem, and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in David’s city.
In the eleventh year of Joram the son of Ahab, Ahaziah began to reign over Judah.
When Jehu had come to Jezreel, Jezebel heard of it; and she painted her eyes, and adorned her head, and looked out at the window.
As Jehu entered in at the gate, she said, “Do you come in peace, Zimri, you murderer of your master?”
He lifted up his face to the window, and said, “Who is on my side? Who?” Two or three eunuchs looked out at him.
He said, “Throw her down!” So they threw her down; and some of her blood was sprinkled on the wall, and on the horses. Then he trampled her under foot.
When he had come in, he ate and drank. Then he said, “See now to this cursed woman, and bury her; for she is a king’s daughter.”
They went to bury her, but they found no more of her than the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands.
Therefore they came back, and told him. He said, “This is Yahweh’s word, which he spoke by his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, ‘The dogs will eat the flesh of Jezebel on the plot of Jezreel,
and the body of Jezebel will be as dung on the face of the field on Jezreel’s land, so that they won’t say, “This is Jezebel.”’”

footnotes.content: Elisha sends a young prophet on a mission with just a vial of oil—a small thing, but God's small things often carry the weight of kingdoms. Notice the prophet doesn't hesitate; obedience doesn't wait for understanding.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The prophet is told to find Jehu and bring him to a private room—God's work often begins in secret. Jehu doesn't know yet what his calling is, but the Lord has already chosen him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I have anointed you king over Israel"—the word comes before the crown, the calling before the throne. The prophet is told to flee after speaking it; his job is only to deliver the word, not to see what comes next.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The young prophet went. That's all—no doubt, no delay. Sometimes the most powerful act of faith is simply to go where you're sent, carrying what you're given.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehu sits among the captains at Ramoth Gilead—a place of conflict, where armies gather. The prophet walks in and chooses to address Jehu alone, "O captain." God's voice often finds us in the midst of our work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Oil poured on his head: a sign of God's choice, though none there understand it yet. Jehu has been chosen long before he felt chosen—the Lord works ahead of our awareness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Strike your master Ahab's house"—Jehu is being called not just to rule, but to execute judgment on Jezebel's house. The Lord uses him as an instrument of justice for the blood of the prophets. A hard calling, but God's.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The house of Ahab will perish utterly—not one will be left. When the Lord brings judgment, it is complete. Righteousness waits a long time, but it does not wait forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ahab's house is compared to Jeroboam and Baasha—kings who turned Israel from the Lord. History whispers warnings to those who listen: idolatry and cruelty carry the same ending.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The dogs will eat Jezebel." The prophetess of Baal will be buried nowhere, remembered by no one—this is what the Lord says to those who lead His people into prostitution and blood. The word of the Lord holds to the end.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When Jehu comes out, his brothers ask if something is wrong—"Is all well?" But Jehu speaks riddles. Those who have touched the word of God often cannot simply say what they've heard; they must live it first.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Finally Jehu tells them plainly: "He said to me, 'Yahweh says, I have anointed you king over Israel.'" Truth spoken aloud becomes flesh. The word moves from the prophet to Jehu to his brothers.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Each man takes his cloak and lays it on the stairs under Jehu—an Eastern custom of homage and coronation. What the prophet whispered in secret, the army now proclaims on the stairs: "Jehu is king."
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehu conspires against Joram, while Joram defends Ramoth Gilead against Syria. So often the one holding the throne doesn't see the judgment coming—he's busy with yesterday's battles.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joram has returned to Jezreel wounded—he's weak, far from his army, waiting to heal. The Lord knows when a throne is most easily shaken. Jehu says no one will escape to warn him; the word comes first, the judgment follows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehu rides hard to Jezreel in his chariot. The time of words is ending; now comes the time of swift, certain action. Those anointed for God's purposes move without hesitation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The watchman on the tower of Jezreel sees a company approaching and calls it out. Jezreel was the seat of Ahab and Jezebel—from its tower, judgment is first sighted, though those inside don't yet know what comes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "What do you have to do with peace? Fall in behind me!" Jehu's answer is clear: the time for asking is past. The messenger doesn't return—he chooses Jehu's side without returning to his master.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A second messenger comes with the same question, the same answer. Jehu gives one chance, then another, but his course doesn't change. He knows what must come to pass.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The watchman knows Jehu's driving style—"he drives furiously." Every person was known in that time, and the watchman reads destiny in the dust on the road. This isn't a stranger coming; this is judgment, and it drives hard.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joram and Ahaziah go out to meet Jehu on Naboth's field—the very land Ahab and Jezebel stole through murder. The Lord draws them to that place. It's not by chance; it's by His hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "What peace, so long as the prostitution of your mother Jezebel and her witchcraft abound?" Jehu speaks the truth that the kingdom has hidden: there is no peace where Jezebel's idolatry and sorcery rule.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In that instant, Joram sees it—"This is treason, Ahaziah!" When the Lord's judgment arrives, suddenly all the king's illusions fall away. The truth is terrible and clear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehu draws his bow with full strength and strikes Joram between the arms, through his heart. One shot, certain. The king who turned Israel from God falls in his own chariot, judgment swift and sure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehu tells Bidkar to throw Joram's body on Naboth's field. He remembers the past: the two of them rode together when Ahab murdered Naboth. Nothing is forgotten by the Lord; the debt comes due in its season.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The blood of Naboth and his sons... I will repay you on this plot." The Lord echoes His word through Jehu: Naboth's innocent blood cries out, and justice is rendered on the very ground where it was shed. God forgets no wrong.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When Ahaziah king of Judah sees Joram's death, he flees toward the garden house—there are place names here: Gur, Ibleam, Megiddo. Each name marks a step of his flight, a step toward his own end. Geography matters in God's judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His servants carry Ahaziah to Jerusalem and bury him with his fathers in David's city. Even in judgment, dignity isn't taken entirely—he receives a burial befitting a king of Judah, though his reign is ended.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the eleventh year of Joram, Ahaziah had reigned—a note of dates and years. Jehu's judgment has rearranged the thrones of both north and south. The word of the Lord reshapes kingdoms.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jezebel hears that Jehu has come. She paints her eyes, adorns her head, and looks from the window—a woman of power to the end, still ruling through beauty and will. She does not grovel; she prepares herself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Do you come in peace, Zimri, you murderer of your master?" Jezebel's taunt cuts like a blade. She throws an insult at her own destroyer, comparing him to Zimri, a usurper. Pride stands unflinching at the edge of the abyss.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehu lifts his face to the window and calls: "Who is on my side?" The eunuchs look out. His question carries the whole matter—will anyone stand with the old order, or with the new?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Throw her down!" Jezebel is thrown from the window; blood sprinkles the wall and the horses, and Jehu tramples her beneath his feet. The woman who prophesied the deaths of God's servants meets her own swift end.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehu goes in and eats and drinks—he sits down in the palace as though nothing remarkable has happened. Only after does he remember Jezebel: "See to this cursed woman and bury her." Even now, she is a woman, a king's daughter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They go to bury her but find only skull, feet, and hands—the dogs have eaten the rest. The prophet's word spoken in secret has come to pass exactly. Not a word falls to the ground.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehu recognizes the fulfillment: "This is Yahweh's word, which he spoke by his servant Elijah." Elijah had spoken it generations before; now Jehu watches it come to pass. Time bends to God's word, not the other way around.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The body of Jezebel will be as dung on the face of the field... so that they won't say, 'This is Jezebel.'" Readers today hear an echo: those who oppose God's people and sorcery eventually fade into nothing, unnamed and forgotten. Judgment is thorough.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
